Investment memo · Nolato (NOLA.B-SE) · 26 November 2026

Nolato: capacity that is already built and paid for should lift earnings by about 30% in two years from a floor valuation, but the brokers' 2027 numbers must fall first

Share price SEK 52.90 · Viewforth model update 2 · money in SEK millions unless stated

#0Summary of key insights, implications and conclusions

The case in one sentence. Nolato is a soundly financed contract manufacturer whose earnings per share should rise by about 30% over two years as capacity it has already built and paid for fills, and its shares sit at the floor of their ten-year valuation range; the open question is timing, because the brokers' 2027 estimates are still too high and Nolato's first two reports of 2027 are more likely to trim those estimates than to raise them.
+30%EPS growth over two years as built, paid-for capacity fills
5 of 5earlier falls of the multiple to about 13x recovered to the median within six months
10 monthsat the floor this time: the longest stay on record
15.0xtwo-year-forward P/E on our earnings, against a headline 13.2x on consensus

The six insights that matter most.

  1. Nolato's profit growth is concentrated in three drivers, but its earnings base is not. Three drivers supply more than all of the profit growth to 2028: one GLP-1 injection-pen programme in Hungary, the proprietary Materials business, and two small acquisitions. The rest of the group is a slight net drag. Yet the three drivers earn under two fifths of 2028 profit, so the failure of any one driver would remove growth, not the earnings base.
  2. 2027 earnings have a floor under them. Close to half of the 2027 profit increase is arithmetic: two acquisitions owned for a full year, and a raw-material cost lag that has already reversed. I put the chance that 2027 EPS falls below 2026 EPS at under 5%.
  3. The risk/reward skew points in opposite directions over the two horizons. For sell-side estimates over the next six months the skew is negative, because consensus already requires our upside case. For the shares over 18 months the skew is positive, because on our lower earnings the stock already trades on a higher multiple than the headline one. The share price discounts something close to our base case, so delivery of that base case would disappoint the brokers more than the shareholders.
  4. The valuation floor has held, and the market is waiting for one proof. The two-year-forward multiple has fallen to about 13x five times in ten years and recovered to its median within six months each time. This time it has stayed at about 13x for ten months, the longest stay on record. The missing proof is evidence that added medical volume earns a normal margin, and two dated reports will supply it: 8 February 2027 and early May 2027.
  5. The first risk to name is the customer, not the device format. The share-price shock at Stevanato on 3 November 2026 was about syringes, whereas Nolato makes parts for multi-dose pens, the format that is gaining share. The under-discussed risk is that Nolato's presumed customer, Novo Nordisk, is losing ground and is pressing its suppliers on price.
  6. Most of the return is a re-rating, so the multiple is the judgement to get right. The Viewforth model shows a total shareholder return of +55% to March 2028 at the guideline multiple of 19.82x. Earnings and dividends alone give about +19%; a return to the ten-year median multiple gives about +33%; a floor case, with earnings 10% short and the multiple back at 13x, gives about (6)% (my calculations, #12).

Five judgements move the value most (the arithmetic is in #9): whether added medical volume earns a normal margin; how fast the Hungarian programme ramps up and at what price; whether Materials keeps growing at 15%; the Swedish krona; and the multiple the market pays once estimates stop falling.

Against Richard's test. The probability of upgrades is not yet unusually skewed to the positive; for the next six months it leans the other way. The skew turns positive once the brokers have reset their estimates, probably by May 2027. From then on our base case is conservative, the comparison quarters are easy, and everything that is in nobody's numbers (bolt-on acquisitions, lower central costs, a strategy plan, portfolio pruning) sits on the upside.

#1Strong/improving tailwinds in the operating environment; and an absence of headwinds/risks

Conclusion: the operating environment is a mild and uneven tailwind: strong and visible for volume in drug delivery and Materials, negative for price, and with the cost headwinds of 2026 now behind the company.

The environment gives Nolato volume and takes back price. Two unrelated external demand drivers are accelerating and two 2026 headwinds are fading, while the presumed customer of the Hungarian programme is pressing its suppliers on price.

Evidence: volume. Medical Solutions' organic growth reached 9% in the third quarter of 2026, its strongest since early 2023, because pharma groups are outsourcing device manufacture to meet the GLP-1 volume wave and newer diagnostics products are helping. Materials, which makes shielding and thermal materials for data centres, satellites and defence, has accelerated in each quarter of 2026. New device regulation (the US Food and Drug Administration's quality rules of February 2026 and the EU's medical device rules) raises the barrier around certified incumbent suppliers such as Nolato.

Evidence: fading headwinds. The raw-material pass-through lag is ending, with the oil price down from about USD 115 to below USD 100. Automotive, the most cyclical end market, has shrunk to about 7% of group sales.

Evidence: price, the building headwind. Novo Nordisk, named by the broker DNB Carnegie as the most likely customer for the Hungarian programme (Nolato has never confirmed the name), cuts its US list prices to USD 675 from January 2027 and has asked device suppliers for cost reductions (Jefferies, July 2026). In October 2026 Novo's US injectable prescriptions fell 5% while Eli Lilly's rose 36%.

Inference. Lower drug prices widen the patient base, which helps a volume supplier, and the device format is on Nolato's side. Multi-dose pens are used worldwide for Ozempic and outside the United States for Wegovy; a US multi-dose Wegovy pen was approved in mid-2026; and Lilly is moving its international markets to a multi-dose pen. Price moves against Nolato, through tiered contracts and renewals.

So what. The environment supports group organic growth of 5-6% a year in 2027-28, against 1-2% in 2023-25, net of a like-for-like price drag of about 0.2-0.5% of revenue a year. The environment is therefore a mild tailwind overall and a strong one in two places.

Against the market. Sector analysts read Stevanato's profit warning as specific to syringes, and I agree. Where I differ is that nobody has connected Novo's weakening position to Nolato in either direction: neither the comfort (pens are the favoured format) nor the concern (Novo's volumes and its cost programme). I also differ from the earlier view in our own work that the krona is a hidden headwind. The krona weakened during 2026, the currency effect on Nolato's sales moved from about (7)% in the first quarter to roughly zero in the third, and brokers mark currency to market at every report. The krona is a swing factor in both directions.

Strongest counter-case. The medical tailwind is one customer's volume. DNB Carnegie expects Novo's traditional pen volumes to decline towards 2030 as pills and next-generation drugs take over. Materials rides a capital-spending theme, and Nolato's last equivalent theme, telecom base stations, ended in a multi-year decline.

What would change my view. Novo's 2027 outlook in early February pointing to lower pen volumes outside the United States; any sign of a supplier tender; Materials growth below 10%; a second oil-price spike.

Score: 61, set by the Rater. Two unrelated external volume drivers are accelerating (Medical organic growth 9% in Q3 on pharma outsourcing of GLP-1 multi-dose pens, the format gaining share; Materials +15/19/27% on data-centre, satellite and defence demand), the raw-material lag and automotive drag are fading and device regulation raises the wall for certified incumbents, lifting group organic growth to 5-6% from 1-2%; net of the direct threat, the presumed customer's price pressure and weakening US position (about 0.2-0.5% of revenue a year), and with consensus sales growth only at the 68th percentile, it is a partial, offset positive in the low 60s, coherent with the External group's 58 but a little higher because two legs are strong and visible.

#2Strong/improving internally-driven corporate change forces; and an absence of problems/risks

Conclusion: the internal change forces are positive and broad, with the heavy lifting (capacity, balance sheet, new management) already done, but their strength is moderate and the cost creep of 2026 shows that they are not free of problems.

The most valuable internal change is already done: Nolato's investment cycle is over. The capacity is built and paid for, a new chief executive has started buying businesses, and almost all of the earnings effect of both changes lies in 2027-28.

Evidence: capacity. Capital spending falls from SEK 788m in 2025 to a guided SEK 600-650m, and the capacity that the spending bought is in place. The Hungarian plant (SEK 600m, with the customer investing about twice that amount alongside) was validated on schedule and has shipped in series since the end of the second quarter of 2026. Further space is ready in Poland, Malaysia and the United States.

Evidence: leadership. Anders Björklund, formerly of Sandvik, became chief executive in July 2026. Within weeks he closed two acquisitions, Unitron and M&M Qualtech (about SEK 600m of sales at group-like margins, for up to about SEK 633m, roughly ten times EBITA), and sold the Romanian unit. The board has added directors who run acquisitive industrial groups, Nolato has appointed a head of strategy and M&A, and the 2026 annual meeting added an organic growth measure to variable pay.

Evidence: the problems. Central costs have risen from about SEK 25m to about SEK 60m a year. Start-up costs cut the Medical margin to 11.3% in the third quarter from 12.1%. Tax, interest and amortisation of acquired intangibles now take about three points more of each krona of EBITA than in 2025. The chief executive held no shares at the end of 2025.

Inference. The internal change is real, well funded and aimed at growth. Because the plant space is already paid for, the next customer programme needs mainly spending on production lines, so the incremental return on that spending should be high.

So what: two options sit outside every forecast, ours included.

Option outside every forecast+5% EPSSEK 1bn of bolt-ons at the 2026 price
A lever on the multiple, not earnings+1.8 pts margin · (13)% EPSExit the ~SEK 3bn industrial business earning ~7%

The balance sheet could fund bolt-on acquisitions: SEK 1bn spent at the 2026 purchase multiple would add about 5% to EPS. The roughly SEK 3bn of industrial business that earns a margin of about 7% is an unpulled lever of an unusual kind: an exit would lift the group margin by about 1.8 points and cut EPS by about 13%. That exit would therefore act on the multiple, not on earnings, and nothing indicates that management will choose it.

Against the market. Brokers welcome the return to M&A, and I agree that the two deals are sensible and fairly priced. I differ on two points. First, the broker ABG expects central costs to normalise, whereas I treat most of the step-up as permanent. There is a small upside here: if the SEK 12m a quarter that DNB Carnegie cites from the chief financial officer is the run-rate of central costs and not the increase, 2027 profit would be SEK 10-18m higher than our base case. Second, the market reads the acquisitions as a strategic step up the value chain; for the next two years they matter as arithmetic, which needs no integration success.

Strongest counter-case. Acquisitions bought at ten times EBITA earn about 8% after tax, close to the cost of capital. Nolato's last large deal (GW Plastics, 2020) diluted margins for years. And a decentralised company is being asked to integrate electronics businesses under a chief executive whose first quarter missed expectations.

What would change my view. Upwards: a strategy update with dated building blocks (I put the chance at 40-50% within 18 months), or central costs at the guided level. Downwards: a deal at 13 times EBITA or more, or a dispute over an earn-out.

Score: 60, set by the Rater. The capacity build is finished and paid for (the Hungarian plant validated on schedule and shipping, capex falling to 600-650), and a new Sandvik-trained CEO has bought two businesses of about SEK 600m sales at group-like margins, sold Romania, added M&A talent and tied pay to organic growth, so internal actions supply most of the 2027-28 profit step; against that, central costs have more than doubled, start-up costs cut the Medical margin and the first quarter under the new CEO missed, so it is real and funded but moderate and not yet shown to work, a little above the Internal group's 57 because the capacity and acquisitions are already in place (the GLP-1 demand itself is counted in topic 1).

#3Value chain, industry structure, business model, financial profile and management

Conclusion: the industry structure, business model and management are sound but average, lifted by an above-average balance sheet and one proprietary niche; together they support steady delivery, not a premium valuation.

Nolato is a medium-quality business with a high-quality balance sheet. Its moat keeps revenue but does not raise price, so the route to outperformance is a re-rating earned by delivering earnings, not a re-rating for quality.

Evidence: the industry protects volume, not price. A validated medical component stays with its supplier for the 10-20 year life of the product, because switching supplier needs 9-18 months of revalidation that the customer pays for. Against that, the buyers are a handful of global pharma groups that dual-source and benchmark cost, and Nolato has no significant contract that binds a customer beyond a year of purchase orders. Nolato is a top-tier specialist, not a leader: large enough to qualify for global programmes, too small to set prices. Its one product-level moat is Materials, which earns margins of at least 20% and about half of Engineered Solutions' profit (DNB Carnegie).

Evidence: the financial profile is mixed. Margins and returns are weaker than at proprietary peers. Capital intensity, debt and earnings quality are better: capital spending is low for the sector because customers fund the tooling, the company expenses development costs, and adjusted and reported profit differ by only SEK 7-14m.

Evidence: management and owners. Management is honest, prudent and good at large projects; our research judged its standards normal, not outstanding. Three founding families control a majority of the votes with about 29% of the capital. The company pays out about 60% of profit and has never bought back a share.

Inference. Because the moat keeps revenue without raising price, the Medical margin is capped near 12-13% and the group margin near 12%.

So what. The fair multiple should be anchored to Nolato's own valuation history, not to the multiples of proprietary product companies. The balance sheet is Nolato's competitive asset: it allowed Nolato to build capacity ahead of demand while its nearest European rival is financially distressed.

Against the market. DNB Carnegie values the group in two parts and applies a medical-sector multiple to Medical Solutions. I agree that the business mix is improving (Medical rises from 57% of sales in 2025 to about 62% by 2030 on our forecasts), and I agree with the brokers on balance-sheet strength. I would not credit pricing power that the business has not shown, which is why our margins flatten where some brokers' margins keep rising.

Strongest counter-case. Nolato's quality may be better than its history says. The single-programme concentration that wrecked 2021-23 has gone, Materials is about a fifth of profit and growing, and work on complete systems carries higher switching costs than work on single components.

What would change my view. Evidence of price increases above cost in medical work; a decision on the low-margin industrial business; or, negatively, a price reset on the Hungarian programme.

Score: 50, set by the Rater. Regulatory revalidation locks in volume for 10-20 years and Materials is a real proprietary niche, but buyers are a few dual-sourcing pharma groups, Nolato is a top-tier specialist that cannot set price, and management is prudent but normal; the financial profile is mixed (ROIC 11.2%, 71st percentile, and clean earnings and low leverage, against an EBITDA margin at the 41st percentile, ROCE 12.4% against 21% in 2019, and the 2021-23 collapse showing low predictability), while new Hungarian capacity should earn well but acquisitions at ten times EBITA earn about the cost of capital. A medium-quality business with a high-quality balance sheet, coherent with the four groups (47, 46, 55, 50).

#4Conservative guidance, expectation management and the track record of delivery

Conclusion: guidance is absent, the targets are ambitious and the record against consensus is poor, so this part of the investment set-up is missing today and will have to be rebuilt by the brokers' own estimate cuts in the first half of 2027.

Nolato's guidance and delivery record is the weakest leg of the case. The mechanism Richard looks for (guide low, beat, raise) does not exist at Nolato, so a conservative base for estimates will have to come from the brokers, not the company.

Evidence. Nolato gives no earnings or revenue guidance, by policy. Its only quantified guidance is for capital spending, which it meets. The cycle targets set in March 2025 have not been met in any period since. Against consensus, the last four quarters were three misses and one soft quarter in a row. Management has called the headwinds "temporary" for three quarters running, and consensus EPS for 2026 has fallen 19% in twelve months.

Inference: management does not manage the brokers down, but the phase is turning. Management's words have been right on direction and early on timing. Two things are changing. The new chief executive's tone is more cautious. And Nolato's misses cluster in ramp-up and input-cost phases (2021-22 and 2026), while its beats cluster in recovery phases (in early 2024 EBITA beat consensus by 21%); 2027 is a ramp-up year without the input-cost drag.

So what. A conservative base for estimates has to come from the brokers cutting their own numbers, which I expect over Nolato's next two reports (#7). With no guidance, every quarterly report tests somebody's model; that is why small misses have moved the shares, and why a clean quarter would move them too.

Against the market. Brokers discount the cycle targets and so do I: on our forecasts the margin target is reached around 2030 and the growth target not at all. I differ from the brokers on timing. Brokers model the 2026 drags reversing at once; management says start-up costs will last "several quarters", and management's record argues for believing the longer reading.

Strongest counter-case. A new chief executive's first full-year report is the natural moment to clear the decks with a Gothenburg restructuring charge (about 40% likely) and a careful outlook. Such a report would hurt reported EPS on the day and would create exactly the rebased expectations that are missing today.

What would change my view. Any quantified outlook; a February report that meets expectations on the lines below EBITDA, where the third-quarter shortfall arose; or, negatively, a third consecutive quarter in which management repeats "temporary" without giving amounts.

Score: 31, set by the Rater. There is no earnings guidance (neutral) and the capex guide is met, but the cycle targets set in March 2025 (above 8% organic growth, above 12% margin, above 15% ROCE) have not been met in any period, the last four quarters were three misses and one soft quarter (EPS 11% short in Q3), 'temporary' has been repeated for three quarters with timing proved early, and consensus 2026 EPS has fallen 19% in a year; the 21% beat of early 2024 and an honest, now more cautious tone keep it off the bottom, but the record is weaker than Indutrade's single miss, coherent with the Guidance (35) and Sell-side (36) groups.

#5Pricing power, operating leverage, financial leverage, cost control and feedback loops

Conclusion: revenue growth does lead to outsized profit growth for the next two years, through operating leverage on capacity that is already paid for; pricing power is the missing lever, and its absence is why the effect fades after 2028.

Profit grows twice as fast as sales to 2028, then the leverage fades. On our forecasts revenue rises 14.6% from 2026 to 2028 and EBITA 28.6%. From 2028 to 2030 the ratio of EBITA growth to revenue growth falls to about 1.4 times (revenue +8.6%, EBITA +12.1%; my calculations).

Evidence: the five mechanisms differ in strength.

  • Operating leverage is material, and weaker on the way up than on the way down. In 2021-23 revenue fell 18% and EBITA halved, a decremental margin of about 32%. For growth we use an incremental margin of 20-25%, for three reasons: the Hungarian contract prices by volume tier, so the unit price falls as the plant fills; start-up costs roll on from Hungary to Malaysia and Poland; and regulated production lines need staff in step with volume. In the third quarter of 2026 Medical Solutions added SEK 158m of sales and only SEK 7m of profit.
  • Pricing power is low. Nolato recovers its costs, with a lag of three to six months. Prices above cost exist only in Materials and in one episode of US repricing in 2024-25. In Medical we assume like-for-like prices fall by 0.5-0.7% a year from 2028.
  • Financial leverage is an option, not a driver. Interest takes about 5% of EBITA.
  • Cost-cutting is defensive. Gross savings of about SEK 40-60m by 2028 are mostly absorbed by wage inflation and new sites.
  • The feedback loops trace an S-curve. Until 2028 the reinforcing loops win: capacity fills, Materials qualifications win the next platform, and a strong balance sheet allows Nolato to build ahead of demand where indebted rivals cannot. From 2028 the balancing loops strengthen: price-downs at contract renewal, working capital absorbed by growth, and new start-ups. The EBITA margin gains by year show the S-curve: 0.8, 0.5, 0.2 and 0.2 points in 2027 to 2030.

Inference. The outsized profit growth of 2027-28 is real and largely mechanical, because the fixed cost of the new capacity is already in the 2026 cost base. The profit growth is a two-year step, not a compounding machine.

So what. Each krona of organic revenue brings about 20 öre of profit for two years, then less. The asymmetry between the 20-25% incremental margin and the 32% decremental margin matters for risk: a revenue shortfall costs more profit than an equal revenue beat adds.

Against the market. The more optimistic brokers assume more operating leverage than we do, and DNB Carnegie believes the Hungarian contract can earn well above the division's historical margin of 13% at scale. I think the tiered pricing hands a good part of the scale gain to the customer by design, and the sell-side discussion does not reflect that.

Strongest counter-case. We may be too cautious. Medical Solutions has earned margins of 13.0-13.6% in five earlier years; Hungary is the sixth expansion of an existing site for an existing customer, not a greenfield plant; and DNB's separate estimate that the contract adds about 1.4 points to the Medical margin at scale matches our 25% incremental margin. If the incremental margin on Hungarian revenue were 35%, 2027 EPS would be about 2% higher (my calculation: SEK 230m of added Hungarian revenue at a ten-point higher incremental margin is SEK 23m of EBITA).

What would change my view. The Medical incremental margin in the next two reports: above 20% would confirm the operating-leverage mechanism; another quarter near 5% would show that start-up costs are outrunning volume.

Score: 53, set by the Rater. Operating leverage is material but asymmetric: capacity whose fixed cost is already in the 2026 base gives an incremental margin of 20-25% against a 10.4% margin, so EBITA grows twice as fast as revenue in 2027-28 (the 2021-23 decremental was 32%), but pricing power is low (cost pass-through with a lag, tiered volume pricing and price-downs of 0.5-0.7% a year), financial leverage is negligible (interest about 5% of EBITA), cost-out is defensive and the loops turn balancing after 2028, so the ratio falls to 1.4x; the ordinary mix, slightly above typical, coherent with Economic strength (55) and Financial forecasts (52).

#6Forecast financials: scope for double-digit growth and for higher growth and margins than the past

Conclusion: the forecasts show double-digit EPS growth in 2027 and 2028 and about 10% a year to 2030, clearly better than the past on growth, margin and cash; the size of the growth is dependable for 2027-28 and thinly supported beyond.

Our base case asks for less than Nolato's own best years. It needs margins that Nolato has earned before, growth below the company's target, and no pricing power, capital-allocation skill or success in mechatronics. Under a third of the gross 2027 EBITA increase rests on a strength that Nolato has not yet shown.

Score: 76, set by the Rater. 10.4% sits just inside the 10-15% B band, and I place it at the floor because the growth is front-loaded (16.5% and 12% in 2027-28, then 7.6% and 6.1%), starts from a down year in 2026, includes about a quarter of the 2025-28 EBITA gain from acquisitions, and the margin only returns to its 2021 level in 2028 and edges above it by 2030; the like-for-like 2025-29 rate would be only about 7%.

#7Scope for upgrades to guidance, sell-side estimates and the narrative over the coming 6-12 months

Conclusion: the scope for upgrades is real but back-loaded: estimate trims of 2-4% are more likely than raises over the next six months, and upgrades become an even bet only from the second half of 2027.

Upgrades come in two phases: likely trims at the next two reports, then an even chance of upgrades from mid-2027. There is no guidance to raise, so all of the scope lies in the brokers' estimates and in the narrative.

Evidence. Consensus 2027 EPS of 3.46 sits above our 3.25, and the four brokers range from 3.33 to 3.82; Nordea is the outlier, and its reasoning is not in our files. The brokers' estimates follow a pattern: they cut the near year and hold the out-year until it becomes the near year. Over twelve months, consensus 2027 EPS is down 8% and consensus 2028 EPS is unchanged.

Inference, phase one: trims are more likely over the next two reports. I put the chance that consensus 2027 EPS is at least 2% lower by the end of May 2027 at about 55%, unchanged at 30% and higher at 15%. I put the chance that actual 2027 EPS reaches today's consensus at about one in five. The cuts should be small, 2-4%, for three reasons: estimates are already well down; DNB Carnegie is within about 6% of us; and perhaps a third of our gap to consensus is a currency assumption that today's exchange rates do not support.

Inference, phase two: from the second half of 2027 the direction of revisions can turn. By then the comparison quarters contain the start-up costs and the raw-material lag, the Hungarian run-rate is visible, and 2028 becomes the near year. I put the chance of positive net revisions at some report between June 2027 and May 2028 at about 50%.

Where the gap to the brokers really sits (my calculation from the brokers' segment figures). The brokers disagree with each other about where the upside lies, and the most careful of them already agrees with us on the part of the case that matters most. Against DNB Carnegie, the lowest of the named brokers, our 2027 EBITA is about SEK 35m lower, at the same group margin. DNB's extra profit comes from about 2.5% more revenue and from lower central costs (about SEK 48m implied, against our 66m). DNB's extra profit does not come from a faster GLP-1 ramp or a richer Medical margin: DNB has a Medical Solutions margin of 12.1% against our 12.0%. Against ABG the gap is about SEK 100m and sits mostly in Medical Solutions, where ABG has segment profit of 850 against our roughly 790.

One caution for monitoring: DNB says that about two fifths of M&M Qualtech's sales are reported in Medical Solutions, whereas our segment build places all of M&M Qualtech's sales there. Group figures are unaffected, but segment growth rates will need care on 8 February.

So what: the upside that is in nobody's numbers.

The narrative has room to move as well, from "show me" to "medical growth with rising free cash flow", once one report is clean.

Against the market. The brokers say that the recovery arrives in 2027 and that the shares are cheap. I say that the recovery is right and that their numbers are about 6% too high. The excess in the brokers' numbers matters less than it looks, because the share price has already tracked the estimates down (#8).

Strongest counter-case. A fourth soft report in February, with a restructuring charge and a cautious outlook, would extend the pattern of misses for another half year and test the valuation floor. The revision that would change the case is not a currency trim but a re-phasing of Hungarian volumes.

What would bring upgrades forward. On 8 February: a Medical margin of 12% or more with Hungarian volumes quantified; Materials growth above 20% again; or a bolt-on acquisition, which would lift sales and EBITDA estimates on the day.

Score: 36, set by the Rater. There is no guidance line to raise, and over the next two reports the memo puts 55% on consensus 2027 EPS falling at least 2% against 15% on a rise, a likely cut of 2-4% against revenue growth of about 6-8% (roughly (0.3) to (0.5) on Richard's rule, with recent revisions at the 30th-35th percentiles); from the second half of 2027 upgrades become an even bet and bolt-ons, lower central costs and a strategy plan sit outside all numbers, and the narrative can move from 'show me' after one clean report, so scope leans negative in the first half and neutral in the second, coherent with the fourth-set group's 36.

Momentum is weak on every measure and collapsing on none. Over twelve months the share price fell by as much as the 2027 estimate, so the multiple has not de-rated further: the shares fell because the earnings estimates did.

#9Riskiness and simplicity of the forecasts and expectations

Conclusion: the case is simple, moderately risky and unusually front-loaded in its uncertainty: growth depends on one customer and two unproven links, but the earnings base is diffuse, the balance sheet removes solvency risk, and the multiple, more than any operating driver, is where the value is decided.

No single operating judgement moves 2027 EPS by more than about 5%; the multiple decides the value. The distance between today's 15.0x and the guideline multiple of 19.82x is worth about 36% of the share price, twice the four operating downsides combined.

Simplicity. The case is simple to state: three drivers, two reports. The case is harder to verify, because the company discloses neither the Hungarian revenue nor a ramp-up schedule, and it describes the middle of the chain from volume to margin in words only.

The range of 2027 EPS outcomes. About four outcomes in five lie between 2.85 and 3.55 around our base of 3.25, roughly (12)% to +9%. That range is about half as wide as Nolato's own experience in 2021-23, when EPS fell 63%. Against our base the skew is mildly negative; against consensus it is strongly negative. Most of the uncertainty is front-loaded: the two items with no outside indicator, the Medical margin and the Hungarian ramp-up, are tested directly on 8 February and in early May 2027.

The five judgements, with the arithmetic. Every SEK 10m of EBITA is SEK 7.75m of net income at a 22.5% tax rate, SEK 0.029 a share on 269.4m shares, or 0.9% of 2027 EPS (my calculations throughout).

Precedents and cyclicality. Nolato's own collapse of 2022-23 came from a single programme that was about a quarter of group sales; the Hungarian programme is about 4% of sales in 2027 and 5-6% at maturity. The sector's slow, dilutive ramp-ups (Stevanato's Indiana plant took two years to reach gross-profit break-even) were greenfield plants for new customers, unlike Hungary. The cyclical part of Nolato is now small, but a further 20% fall in automotive sales would still cost about 3.5-4% of EPS.

Downside in the shares. At the five-year low multiple of 12.35x on our earnings the shares would be worth about SEK 44, 17-18% below the model's price. A stressed case (a Hungarian delay, a stronger krona and weaker automotive sales together) points to SEK 35-36.

#10Where the stock is in its lifecycle

Conclusion: the stock is bottoming and on the cusp of turning up; a broadening of the thesis is a plausible late-2027 development, not a description of today.

I judge the stock to be bottoming and close to turning up, one or two stages earlier than the dashboard's computed phase of Broadening. The phase matters because it sets the guideline multiple (#11).

Evidence. Fundamentals have turned in Medical and Materials. Estimates are still falling and sell-side momentum is D. The multiple is at its floor and has not left it (#11). No broker has raised its numbers since the turn began.

Inference. The stock is not stalling or collapsing: organic growth is accelerating, the drags are identified and reversing, and the share price has stopped falling faster than the estimates. The stock is not yet broadening or reinforcing: those phases need rising estimates and several drivers visible in the numbers, whereas today the estimates are falling and the acquisitions mask the fall.

The sequence I expect, with dates. The stock turns up by mid-2027 if the February and May reports show the Medical margin recovering and 2027 estimates stop being cut. It broadens from late 2027 into 2028 if the Hungarian programme reaches its run-rate, Materials holds double-digit growth, and a bolt-on acquisition or a strategy plan adds a new leg. Nolato's last cycle ran the same way: estimates stopped falling in late 2023 and the shares' recovery ran on to mid-2024 (#11).

So what. If the stock is in Broadening, the 80th-percentile multiple applies now; if the stock is bottoming, that multiple belongs to a phase it has yet to reach.

Against the market. Brokers describe a recovery already under way, whereas the share price describes a stock on probation. I side with the share price on timing and with the brokers on direction.

Strongest counter-case. The dashboard may be seeing something real. In fundamentals the thesis has broadened, from a single margin-repair story in 2023-25 to medical growth, Materials, acquisitions and a cash-flow inflection, and the shares are above their 200-day average. On that reading only the estimates lag, and estimates are the last thing to turn.

What would change my view. Towards turning up: the first report after which 2027 EPS estimates hold. Back towards stalling: a second quarter of Medical growth without margin improvement, or a re-phasing of the Hungarian ramp-up.

Score: 52, set by the Rater. I agree with the memo, not the computed Broadening: fundamentals have turned in Medical and Materials and the price has stopped falling faster than the estimates, but 2027 estimates are still being cut, sell-side momentum is weak and the multiple has not left its floor, so it is Bottoming close to Turning, with the turn dated to the February and May 2027 reports; like Greggs (a computed Broadening that is really bottoming, capex past its peak) but with revisions still falling, unlike Solid State's steady ones offset by accelerating organic growth.

#11The fair multiple

Conclusion: the guideline multiple of 19.82x is a credible ceiling for a delivered recovery but sits a phase ahead of the evidence; 16-17x is the fair multiple I would defend for the next 12-18 months.

On our earnings the stock is on 15.0x, not the headline 13.2x, and the multiple the evidence supports for the next 12-18 months is 16-17x. The guideline fair multiple is 19.82x two-year-forward earnings, the 80th percentile of the stock's ten-year history, set for the Broadening phase.

Evidence from the stock's own history (monthly dashboard series; my reading).

  • The ten-year range of the two-year-forward multiple runs from 13.3x at the 10th percentile through a median of 16.9x to 19.2x at the 75th percentile. The top of the range was set in 2017-18 and 2020-21, when a single vaporiser programme and pandemic demand drove growth that has since gone.
  • The multiple last printed at or above 19.8x in December 2021. Its high since then is 19.2x, in May 2024, at the peak of a run of earnings beats.
  • The multiple has touched about 13x five times before (January 2017, December 2018, March 2020, October 2022, July 2023). Each time it was back at the median within one to six months, and in four of the five cases it reached 19x or more within ten months. From the July 2023 trough the shares rose 47% in ten months; from the December 2018 trough, 59% in six months.
  • The present stay at 13.0-14.3x has lasted since February 2026, more than three times as long as the longest earlier stay.

Inference: three points.

  1. The guideline multiple is reachable, but it is the multiple of a delivered recovery. History shows the stock reaching 19-20x at the top of each recovery, after estimates turned and beats accumulated. 19-20x is not the multiple of a stock whose estimates are still being cut. For the phase I see (#10), a fair multiple over the next 12-18 months is 16-17x, around the ten-year and five-year medians.
  2. The headline cheapness overstates the cushion. At 13.2x on consensus the stock looks to be on its floor; on the earnings I believe in, it is on 15.0x, between the 25th percentile and the median of the last five years. About 1.8 points of the apparent discount is the market disbelieving consensus, not the market undervaluing the company.
  3. The guideline multiple is less stretched than it looks once the earnings bases are aligned. The historical percentiles are measured on consensus earnings, whereas the model applies 19.82x to our lower earnings. The same target share price would be about 18.4x on today's consensus (my calculation: 19.82 x 3.53 / 3.80), near the 90th percentile of the last five years and between the median and the 75th percentile of the last ten.

So what. I would treat 16-17x as the fair multiple that the evidence supports today, and 19.8x as the multiple the stock can earn if 2027 delivers and upgrades begin; I put the chance of that outcome at roughly one in three within 18 months. The difference between the two multiples is worth about 22 points of return (#12).

Against the market. The brokers' targets (mean SEK 64.8, twelve months out) imply about 17x the brokers' own earnings: close to my fair multiple, but on higher numbers. DNB Carnegie's bull case needs 10% sales growth and a 12.6% margin for its highest multiple; neither is in our forecasts.

Strongest counter-case, for a higher multiple. Every earlier exit from 13x overshot the median, and three things are better now than at those troughs: no single programme dominates, free cash flow is inflecting towards a 5-6% yield, and the medical share of profit is higher. For a lower multiple: slow growers in this industry are punished twice, and if consensus merely converges on our numbers, the multiple on consensus rises by about 1.8 points with no change in the share price.

What would change my view. Up, towards the guideline multiple: two clean reports and the first upgrades. Down, towards 14-15x: a price reset on the Hungarian programme, which would cap the margin story.

Score: 86, set by the Rater. Cheap on both measures gives A, but part of the cheapness is deserved: both readings use a consensus the memo expects to fall about 6%, and on the memo's earnings the stock is on 15.0x, below the ten-year median of 16.9x but not at its floor, which takes the peer reading to only about 5% cheaper than normal (neutral), and the top of the ten-year range was set by a vaporiser programme and pandemic demand that have gone; so I move it one step to B and place it high in the band because the own-range cheapness is robust (the floor has held five times) and the memo's fair multiple of 16-17x is still above today's.

#12Total shareholder return

Conclusion: the model's returns of +55% to March 2028 and +70% to September 2029 are about three fifths and under one half re-rating respectively; earnings and dividends alone give about +19% and +32%, so the return is attractive without the guideline multiple and exceptional only with it.

The return has a dependable core of about +19% to March 2028 and a large contingent layer that needs a re-rating. On the outcomes I find most plausible, the asymmetry is roughly +33% against (6)%, with the guideline return of +55% as the reward for full delivery.

What drives each part of the return.

  • The multiple (+32.1 points at both horizons). The re-rating from 15.0x to 19.82x is assumed complete by March 2028 and held thereafter. It is almost three fifths of the first-horizon return and a one-off gain, which is why the annualised return falls from 39% to 21% as the horizon lengthens. The re-rating depends on the phase moving to Broadening (#10) and on the fifth judgement in #9.
  • Earnings (+12.6 and +21.1 points). Two-year-forward EPS rises from about 3.53 today to about 3.97 at the first horizon and 4.27 at the second, some 7-9% a year. That rise is the three-driver recovery of #6, and its plausible error is about a tenth either way (#9).
  • Dividends (+6.5 and +10.4 points). Dividends of SEK 1.60, 1.85 and 2.05 a share give a yield of 3-4% a year at a payout ratio of about 60%, covered by free cash flow from 2027.

Inference: the return comes in three layers.

  • The core, about 10-14% a year, needs only our earnings and the dividend at an unchanged multiple.
  • The middle layer, another 14-15 points, needs the multiple to return to its ten-year median, which it has done after every earlier trough.
  • The top layer, a further 22-24 points, needs the guideline multiple, and the guideline multiple needs upgrades.
  • The floor case loses about 6%.

Timing within the 6-18 months. The path of the return is unlikely to be even. If the first reports of 2027 bring estimate trims, the first six months may deliver little beyond the dividend; the re-rating, if it comes, is an event of the second half of 2027 and of 2028.

Against the market. The brokers' mean target implies about +22% over twelve months before the dividend, on earnings I think are too high and a multiple I think is fair. My value at the median multiple for March 2028, about SEK 67 before dividends, is near the brokers' targets, but it is reached later and on lower earnings.

Strongest counter-case. The return is mostly re-rating, the re-rating depends on a phase change that has not happened, and the company's habit of small misses is what has kept the multiple at its floor.

What would change my view. A February report that moves the multiple off its floor would shift the probability weight towards the higher rows of the table; a re-phased Hungarian ramp-up would shift it towards the floor case.

Score: 81, set by the Rater. About +30% sits in the B band (27% about 82, 35% about 90), and the three-year check is supportive; I place it low in the band because the path runs through a re-rating (earnings and dividends alone give about +19%), the first six months may deliver little beyond the dividend, and the lower tail reaches (6)% in the floor case and SEK 35-36 in the stressed case.

#13Summary conclusion on the business and its investment case

Nolato is a better business than its last five years suggest and a less certain one than its brokers suggest. The capacity is built, the balance sheet is strong, and three identifiable drivers should lift EPS by about 30% in two years, with close to half of the first year's increase near-certain. The business model limits how far the improvement goes: it keeps volume and gives back price, so the margin flattens near 12% and growth fades to mid-single digits after 2028.

The case is interesting because of the gap between two sets of expectations. The brokers' numbers are too high, and with no guidance to anchor them, the next two reports are more likely to cut those numbers than to raise them. The share price, by contrast, already discounts something close to our base case and sits where the multiple has turned five times in ten years. The estimate skew is therefore unfavourable for six months and the share-price skew favourable over 18 months, and the reports of 8 February and early May 2027 decide which skew matters more.

The single thing to watch
  • Whether added medical volume comes through at a normal margin
The single thing to fear
  • News about the presumed customer's volumes or prices

Most of the return lies in the multiple, and the multiple will follow the first report after which estimates stop falling.

Thesis's Change Forces' Strength63

Thesis's Change Forces' Strength: 63, set by the Rater. Both input forces are clearly but moderately positive (external 61: two accelerating volume legs offset by customer price pressure; internal 60: paid-for capacity, a new acquisitive CEO, offset by cost creep), and they reach profits fairly surely (close to half the 2027 increase is arithmetic) but only to EPS growth of about 10% a year, near the Universe median and front-loaded, which is the low-to-mid-60s case the levels describe, in line with the memo's C.

Foundations' Robustness52

Foundations' Robustness: 52, set by the Rater. Quality is typical (50): long regulatory lock-in on installed programmes, a proprietary Materials niche, clean earnings and a strong balance sheet, against a price-taker position, contract-manufacturer margins, below-target returns and a 2021-23 collapse that shows limited predictability; the poor recent delivery record (31) keeps it from rising towards Judges Scientific's 60, but the non-discretionary medical core and low leverage keep it at about typical.

Setups' Fit/Crispness63

Setups' Fit/Crispness: 63, set by the Rater. The case fits 'Major CfC Clearing in MQ non-cyclical or better business on Q1 multiple, leading to reversion to normal' (CfC: cause for concern; MQ: medium-quality; Q1: first-quartile) in kind: a medium-quality business on a first-quartile multiple with identified, sized concerns (start-up costs, the raw-material lag, misses) clearing through 2027; but the concern is moderate rather than major, about a third of the business is cyclical, and today's problems (cost creep, a Medical margin still falling, a CEO whose first quarter missed) blur the clearing, so it sits at the low end of Richard's 65-75 for a CfC clearing in a middling business; that the clearing is not yet in estimates is not counted here.

Case Riskiness52

Case Riskiness: 52, set by the Rater. Over topic 9's 50: the case is simple to state, the earnings base is diffuse, leverage is low and the multiple sits at the floor of its range (limiting de-rating risk, which Richard counts in favour), but most risks are more than paper cuts: growth depends on one unconfirmed customer with a sudden-headline risk, there is no guidance and no management of sell-side expectations, a run of misses, four brokers and an illiquid stock, so the equity outcome is less predictable than the operating lines.

How to read this page

Every rating of this stock on one page: the Rater's 1-100 number, its letter and the Rater's own reason (at most three sentences, taken from the ratings file; nothing newly written). The number is the company's approximate standing in the Universe of about 1,300 listed European companies (90 = better than about 9 in 10; 50 = typical). A letter follows its item's rule: rank among the stocks scored (A the top 10%; B+ and B the next 15%; C+, C and C- the next 25%; D the next 25%; F the bottom 25%); or Richard's cut-offs on the measure for the four numerical topics (forecast financials, current momentum, the fair multiple, total shareholder return). On the change-forces items the number carries a sign (50 = neither positive nor negative) and the letter is the rank, so read the two together. "9th of 30 stocks scored" is the stock's place on that item. A dashed badge is provisional (fewer than 30 stocks scored).
